configs.description: EX2200-24P-4G - 24 10/100/1000 PoE+ ports and four SFP uplinks, built-in AC supply, two built-in fans and a third in the supply, side-to-rear airflow, 405 W for PoE (Table 3).
configs.name: ac

gaps.note: Table 31 lists the supplied two-post mounting brackets (EX2200: provided) and a separately orderable four-post rack-mount kit with 2-inch recess front brackets, and gives no part number for the kit; no figure measures a bracket position, so no ear position is stated and no kit is listed.
gaps.wanted: The four-post rack-mount kit's part number and a dimensioned drawing of the bracket positions.

gaps.note: No photograph of any EX2200 is held and the maker's image library no longer carries one; both faces are read from the guide's figures alone, which are line drawings, so colour, finish, the printing on the front (model name, logo, port numerals) and the legends on the rear are not confirmed.
gaps.wanted: Straight-on studio photographs of the EX2200-24P front and rear.

gaps.note: The jack lamps carry the component's link and activity vocabulary; the guide's Status lamp switches meaning with the mode button and no per-lamp state list fits the component.

airflow.note: the cooling system provides side-to-rear chassis cooling (Figure 15 for PoE models): air enters by the side vents and leaves by the rear openings. The chassis enum has no side-to-rear value, so the side value is carried.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: Hardware guide, Power Supply in EX2200 Switches: "The power supply in EX2200 switches is built in along the rear panel of the chassis"; Table 4 lists "Built-in power supply" and the cooling system is two fans along the rear plus, on PoE models, a third fan in the supply whose air leaves by the third opening (Figure 15). Nothing in the guide describes removing or replacing any of them. They are part of the chassis, not bays and not components.

chassis.note: Table 5: height 1.75 in (4.45 cm), width 17.5 in (44.5 cm) and 19 in (48.2 cm) with the mounting brackets attached, depth 10.5 in (26.7 cm), weight 8 lb (3.6 kg) for the EX2200-24P. 445.0 x 44.45 x 267.0 is carried: width and depth as the printed metric, the height as the 1U pitch Table 31 gives (1.75 in). The figures draw no ears, and the jack pitch closing on the registry at that width says the figure is the body.

colour.note: borrowed - the chassis #919599 and the jack shells #b1b2b5 are the EX2300 front photograph's medians. The guide's figures are line drawings with no colour and no EX2200 photograph is held, so these are a relative's and not a reading of this device.

front-layout.note: estimated - read off Figure 2 as described under gate-1. The 24 jacks stand in two shells of six columns at 187.3 and 277.4 mm, the first jack at 190.6 mm, the jack pitch the registry's 13.97 and a 6.27 gutter (shell step 90.1 mm), the shell boxes 89.0 mm wide, rows 14.85 mm apart, the upper row turned 180 so its lamp tabs are above as the figure shows. The four uplink cages abut on the registry's 14.25 pitch from 366.1 mm and stand 27.4 mm down. The left half of the face is blank in the figure. A long recessed slot runs along the top edge from 7.1 to 438.1 mm; it carries no printing. The guide's figure draws four small oval marks along the top edge, no vents, no model name and no logo on the front, so none is drawn and no logo zone is reserved: the real unit's printing is not known from any source held. The chassis and shell colours are borrowed from the EX2300 photographs (see colour).

gate-1.note: Figure 2 was rendered at 600 dpi and measured with a pixel ruler, together with Figure 1 whose front face it shares. The 48-port figure's front face is 2430 px across and 237 px down: 5.467 px per mm across from the 445 mm of Table 5 and 5.34 down from 44.45 mm, a 2.4 percent aspect error, so x and y are each taken from their own dimension and every position is estimated and good to about a millimetre. The jack width reads 12.7 mm, the registry's 12.7 for the ganged RJ-45 cell, on a quantity the scale never saw. The figures are perspective views from above and the front face is the near rectangle; Figure 5 (rear) is a flat elevation, 2722 px across and 266 down: 6.124 px per mm across and 5.99 down, a 2.2 percent aspect error. Figure 2's two shells stand where the last two of Figure 1 do (186.8 mm measured, 187.3 drawn).

lamps.note: Hardware guide, Tables 6 to 10 and Figures 7, 11 and 12. Each RJ-45 port and uplink has two lamps, Link/Activity and Status; Figure 11 puts them on the two tabs of the jack. The Status lamp reads out whichever of speed (SPD), duplex (DX), administrative status (EN) and PoE (POE) the Factory Reset/Mode button has selected, shown by which port-mode lamp is lit; the POE lamp reads PoE status on this model (Table 10 lists it for the EX2200-24P). SYS is green and ALM unlit, amber or red. The jack lamps keep the component's link and activity vocabulary because a block cannot override it per lamp. Figure 12 draws the uplink lamps as two circles either side of each numeral; the left is taken as Link/Activity and the right as Status, which no figure confirms, so it is estimated. The SYS and ALM lamps are drawn as the figure draws them, oblong, and their legends tilted in the figure are printed level here.

port-numbering.note: drawing - Figure 2 prints each column's two numbers above its shell, the even number up and left of a short divider and the odd number down and right (0 and 1, 2 and 3, ... 22 and 23), and the four uplinks 0 to 3 between their two lamps. Both numbers of a column are printed above the upper jack, so which jack takes which is by analogy with the EX2300 faceplate (the upper jack takes the even number), estimated. The even numeral is drawn 2.55 mm left of its jack's centre and the odd one on its centre, as measured on Figure 1; the small divider lines between them are not drawn. Port numbers are as printed, from 0. The Junos interface names are not printed: Table 4 gives PIC 0 as 24x10/100/1000BASE-T and PIC 1 as 4x GE SFP, i.e. ge-0/0/0 to ge-0/0/23 and ge-0/1/0 to ge-0/1/3; they are recorded here and not in an interfaces block because the faceplate does not print them.

power.note: Table 11: maximum power consumed by the switch 60 W when no PoE power is drawn, 204.6 BTU/hour, and maximum PoE power available 405 W; Table 12: AC input 100 through 240 VAC, 50/60 Hz, 7 A at 100 VAC and 2.9 A at 230 VAC for switches with ports equipped for PoE. The maximum PoE power per port is 30 W on Junos OS 10.3 and later (15.4 W before), Power Supply in EX2200 Switches.

rear-layout.note: estimated - positions read off Figure 5 (labelled EX2200-24-4G) as described under gate-1: the management jack with the USB port under it in one housing, the RJ-45 console port, the RPS port (a rounded plate with a slotted opening and four screws), the two-hole earthing plate with the earth symbol, the ESD point, three round exhaust openings, the two small slots at 270 mm and the AC inlet, which the guide names in that order. The three openings are drawn at 142.0, 192.2 and 236.9 mm; their uneven spacing is the figure's. The guide says the two left openings have fans and the third has none and is exposed on PoE models, so all three are drawn as vent fields here, and the screw the figure shows at the third opening's upper left (non-PoE rear) is not drawn because the exposed opening covers it. The serial number ID label is a paper label carrying a real serial number and is not drawn; the power cord retainer clips are accessories and are not drawn. Figure 5 prints no legend near the inlet, so none is drawn. The jack housing is one dark recess behind the management and USB ports.

rps-port.note: estimated - the RPS port (Figure 5 callout, guide list of rear panel components) is drawn as chassis art: the plate and its opening at 50.1 to 118.0 mm and four screws. It is not a component: the library has no RPS connector and its DCIM export has no row for one. The guide names no RPS part number and no document of the RPS is held.

sources.note: EX2200 and EX2200-C Switches Hardware Guide, Juniper Networks, published 2022-02-02 (268 pages), the copy held in Juniper's EX documentation archive (https://www.juniper.net/documentation/en_US/release-independent/downloads/ex-series/ex-series-doc-archives.zip, member ex-series-doc-archives/ex2200.pdf): Figure 2 (24-port front), Figure 5 (rear), Table 3 (models), Table 5 (chassis size and weight), Tables 6 to 10 (LEDs), the cooling system section with Figures 14 and 15, Tables 11 to 13 (power) and Table 16 (environment). The guide is the only source held for the EX2200: Juniper's datasheet is dehosted, and the maker's image library and the held photograph set have no EX2200 photograph. The guide carries Juniper's copyright and reserves its rights, so its figures were read for what is on each face and where, and none was copied; every skin here is drawn from those measurements.

uplinks.note: drawing - one row of four built-in SFP cages numbered 0 to 3 (Figure 2); the guide gives 1-gigabit SFP transceivers for fibre and copper and says an SFP uplink can be configured as a Virtual Chassis port. PoE is not available on the uplink ports.
